# SpamHell

> Satirical counter-tool against voice phishing. Turns a short text into "spam style" (스팸체): Hangul jamo splitting, dots between syllables, digit substitution, noise symbols, spam header/footer. Same seed gives the same output in every implementation.

SpamHell never sends messages. The web demo only opens the user's own SMS app with a prefilled draft; the user presses send. There is no bulk, batch, or automatic sending, and templates do not impersonate real institutions.

## Use it

- Web demo: https://leejongyoung.github.io/SpamHell/
- JavaScript/TypeScript: npm `spamhell` (`toSpam`, `toKorean`, `getTemplate`)
- CLI: npm `spamhell-cli` (command `spamhell`; the Python package ships the same command)
- Python: package in the repository under packages/python (PyPI release pending): `to_spam`, `to_korean`, `get_template`
- AI assistants (MCP, stdio): npm `spamhell-mcp` with tools `spamhell_transform`, `spamhell_template`, `spamhell_list_templates`, `spamhell_reply` (pick the situation id that best matches an incoming scam message, then get a satirical reply), `spamhell_list_situations` (ids, labels, descriptions, example incoming messages)
- Situation replies: `spamhell --situation <id>` (list with `--list-situations`), `getReply(id)` in JS, `get_reply(id)` in Python

## Source

- Repository: https://github.com/leejongyoung/SpamHell (Apache-2.0)
